reason: `Literal(Decimal("NaN"), XSD_DECIMAL)` is stored as `Literal("NaN", XSD_DECIMAL)` and round-trips equal through four text formats, while the plain `Decimal("NaN")` raises `ProvValueError` saying it has no xsd:decimal form. #482 and the Python values section of `docs/reference/values.md`.

A plain value has the same value key as the typed `Literal` twin the writers would write, and a different key from a Literal of another datatype, a float against an int, a bool against an int and a datetime against a Literal. #663, #235 and #34, and the Equality section of `docs/reference/values.md`.

A document asserting a subclass of int, float, datetime or aware datetime serialises in each round-trip format without the subclass name, reads back as the plain type equal to the original, and holds one value when subclass and plain value are both asserted. #657 and #663.

The first slot of the value key is the type for a `QualifiedName`, an `Identifier` and a `Decimal`. Spec 5 section 4.3 (#690) keeps `type(value)` in the key of an Identifier and of a value with no plain form.

`Literal("hi", langtag=tag).langtag` equals the tag and warns nothing for `None`, `en`, `EN`, `en-GB`, `zh-Hant-TW`, `de-CH-1901` and `x-private`. Conformance caveat C6 says a tag of letters followed by hyphen-led groups of letters and digits is accepted.

A document holding `Literal("hi", langtag="en-US")` reads back from PROV-JSON, PROV-XML and PROV-JSON-LD equal to the original with no warning. Conformance caveat C6 accepts a BCP 47 tag, and #472 rejects only a tag of another shape.

A typed literal in canonical spelling (`5` int, `true` boolean, `1.5` double, `5000000000` long, `INF` double, ` 5\n` int) is stored as the Python value. The Python values section of `docs/reference/values.md` stores a literal with the datatype and spelling prov writes for a plain value as that value, and #235 and #527.
`Literal("x", datatype, tag)` raises `ProvValueError` naming the datatype for a str, an object and an `Identifier` datatype, with a tag `en` and with none. #705.

Under a decimal context of precision 1 with InvalidOperation untrapped, `Literal("1.0", XSD_DECIMAL)` still equals `Literal("1.00", XSD_DECIMAL)` with equal hashes, and `sNaN` differs from `NaN` and equals itself. #595 and #593.

`Literal(10, XSD_DECIMAL)` equals `Literal(10.0, XSD_DECIMAL)` and `Literal("10.00", XSD_DECIMAL)` with equal hashes, and differs from `Literal("10.01", XSD_DECIMAL)`. #77 asks for xsd:decimal literals to compare by value, and the Equality section of `docs/reference/values.md` says the same. Later audit: its pairs could become rows of `SAME_VALUE` and `DIFFERENT_VALUE`, which check both orders and the hash; it is the named test for #77, so a merge keeps that link.
PROV-JSON text with `"lang": ""` raises `ProvJSONException` saying record 'ex:e1' has an empty language tag, caused by a `ProvValueError`. #472 and conformance caveat C5.
`Literal("hi", langtag="")` raises `ProvValueError` saying the language tag of 'hi' is empty. #472 and conformance caveat C5.

Merged into the row `float-subclass` of test_literal_semantics.py::test_literal_spells_a_python_value_in_xsd_form. `Literal.__init__` reaches `_literal_text`, whose `float.__repr__` call spells a float subclass with its own repr as `0.1` under `xsd:decimal`. A planted `repr(value)` fault there fails only the merged row, and the row also asserts the datatype.

Merged into two rows, `"abc"` against `"abc"` in `SAME_VALUE` and `"abc"` against `"abd"` in `DIFFERENT_VALUE`, both as `xsd:decimal`. They are read by test_literal_semantics.py::test_two_spellings_of_one_value_are_equal and test_literal_semantics.py::test_two_values_are_not_equal. `_decimal_value` rejects both texts and `xsd_value` returns None, so `Literal._key` keys each literal by its text, and `Literal.__eq__` and `Literal.__hash__` compare that key. The `SAME_VALUE` row asserts equality in both orders and equal hashes, and the `DIFFERENT_VALUE` row inequality in both orders, a superset of the removed test's assertions, and a planted fault in `_decimal_value` that returned `Decimal(0)` or raised was still caught (#527).

`Literal("True", XSD_BOOLEAN)` and `Literal("inf", XSD_DOUBLE)` are kept and compare as text through four text formats and read back from PROV-O as `True` and `inf`. The Equality section of `docs/reference/values.md` says a text outside the lexical space compares as text, and conformance caveat C10 records what rdflib coerces on read.

Two `xsd:integer` literals of 5000 digits compare equal when the text is the same and unequal when one text has an extra digit, without raising. The Equality section of `docs/reference/values.md` says a text with no value in its datatype compares as text, and this test guards against a raise on a long integer text.

An entity holding `Literal("hello", langtag="EN")` serialises to PROV-JSON containing `"lang": "EN"` and to PROV-O N-Triples containing `"hello"@EN`. #259 leaves the stored tag as written, so output keeps its case (docs/reference/conformance.md, Literals table, the tag as given). The maintainer added the PROV-O case because a fault that lowercased the tag in `literal_rdf_representation` passed the whole suite, and the new case fails under it.

`Literal("hello", langtag="EN")` equals `Literal("hello", langtag="en")` with equal hashes and differs from the same text tagged `fr`. #259 and the Equality section of `docs/reference/values.md`, which say language tags compare case-insensitively.
`Literal("hi", langtag=tag)` raises `ProvValueError` naming the tag for `en_US`, `1en`, `en-`, `en--US`, `en US` and `fr-ç`. #472 and conformance caveat C6.

Reading PROV-JSON, PROV-XML or PROV-JSON-LD text whose tag was edited to `en_US` raises the reader's own error naming the record and `'en_US'`, caused by a `ProvValueError` and not itself a `ValueError`. #472 and conformance caveat C6, which reject the tag from any format.

`Literal(value, datatype)` has the XSD lexical text and datatype given in each row, for bool, float, Decimal, datetime, int, str, timedelta, UUID, bytes, date, an int Enum and a bytes value under `xsd:duration` (the Python values section of `docs/reference/values.md`, #525, #527 and #656). It also holds the row `float-subclass`, folded in from `test_literal_semantics.py::test_float_subclass_with_a_custom_repr_converts_to_decimal`. A float subclass with its own repr given `xsd:decimal` spells as `0.1`, because `_literal_text` calls `float.__repr__`. A verifier's planted fault that called `repr(value)` there failed only this row, and the row adds the datatype assertion the removed test lacked. Nothing is lost from the removed test.
`Literal("NaN", XSD_DOUBLE)` is stored as a float NaN, and two documents built the same way compare equal. The Equality section of `docs/reference/values.md` says a NaN is one value with itself.

A typed literal with a non-canonical text (`05` int, `+5` long, `1e0` double, `1.0` float, `1` boolean, `1.00` decimal) keeps its text through four text formats and reads back from PROV-O as the second column, with the document equal in every format. #527 and the Python values and Equality sections of `docs/reference/values.md`, and conformance caveat C10 for the PROV-O column.
An entity holding the plain string `"hello"` serialises to N-Triples (`rdf_format="nt11"`) with no `^^` in the output. #89 asks for one canonical form for a string literal, the plain literal.

After an entity holds `Literal("05", XSD_INT)`, `add_attributes({"ex:a": 5})` leaves one value and the stored value is still `Literal("05", XSD_INT)`. #527 and the Equality section of `docs/reference/values.md`, which make `5` and `Literal("05", XSD_INT)` one value.

Each pair of two spellings of one value in an XSD datatype (integer family, float, double, boolean, decimal, with or without surrounding whitespace) compares equal in both orders with equal hashes (#527, #593, #594, #595, and the Equality section of `docs/reference/values.md`). It also holds the row `"abc"` against `"abc"` as `xsd:decimal`, folded in from `test_literal_semantics.py::test_ill_formed_decimal_literals_compare_lexically`. `_decimal_value` rejects that text and `xsd_value` returns None, so `Literal._key` keys the literal by its text, and `Literal.__eq__` and `Literal.__hash__` compare that key. The row keeps the original's equality and hash assertions and adds the reversed order, and a verifier's planted fault that made `_decimal_value` raise on an ill-formed text failed it. Nothing is lost from the removed test.

Each pair of literals that differ in datatype, in value, or by a text outside its lexical space or range compares unequal in both orders (#235, #527, #593, #594, #595, and the Equality section of `docs/reference/values.md`). It also holds the row `"abc"` against `"abd"` as `xsd:decimal`, folded in from `test_literal_semantics.py::test_ill_formed_decimal_literals_compare_lexically`. `_decimal_value` rejects both texts and `xsd_value` returns None, so `Literal._key` keys each literal by its text, and `Literal.__eq__` compares that key, so they differ. A verifier's planted fault that made `_decimal_value` return `Decimal(0)` for an ill-formed text failed this row and passed the `1e1` against `10` row, so the row does its own job. Nothing is lost from the removed test.

A typed literal of another datatype than prov writes, a non-canonical spelling or a datatype with no plain form is stored as a `Literal` with its text and datatype. #235 and the Python values section of `docs/reference/values.md`.

`Literal.__setstate__` raises `ProvValueError` for a state with an empty tag, a tag `en_US`, or a datatype that is not a `QualifiedName`. Conformance caveats C5 and C6 and #705 say no literal the writers cannot spell may exist, from any route.
